newsitem.title: CHINA: Gas explosion kills 12 at private China mine.
newsitem.headline: Gas explosion kills 12 at private China mine.

text.p: A gas explosion at a private coal mine in southwestern China killed 12 miners and injured six, said an edition of the Yangcheng Evening News seen in Beijing on Friday.

The latest deadly explosion in China's accident-plagued mining industry occurred on May 7 at the Lifa coal mine in Zhijin county in southwestern Guizhou province, the newspaper said. It gave no reason for the delay in reporting the disaster.
The newspaper blamed the explosion on the mines's ventilation system, which was below standard, but gave no further details.
Local authorities detained the owner of the mine, who had recruited local farmers since March without government approval, it said.
China said this week it would sack directors of coal mines if accidents in their mines killed 10 or more people, to try to boost safety in China's poorly regulated and often dangerous mines.
A gas explosion this month at a coal mine in eastern Shandong province killed 31 miners in a blast blamed on the mine's ventilation system.
China has issued a string of directives to try to improve safety in its mines where explosions and accidents, mainly at improperly maintained village level mines, kill up to 10,000 miners each year.
